policy_title: Reduce Child Poverty and Reform Universal Credit
stated: Labour will develop an ambitious strategy to reduce child poverty, working with various sectors. Initial steps include introducing free breakfast clubs in every primary school, protecting renters from arbitrary eviction, slashing fuel poverty, banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, and improving employment support. The party is committed to reviewing Universal Credit to make work pay and tackle poverty, aiming to end mass dependence on emergency food parcels.

source.quote: Child poverty has gone up by 700,000 under the Conservatives, with over four million children now growing up in a low-income family. Labour will develop an ambitious strategy to reduce child poverty. We will work with the voluntary sector, faith organisations, trade unions, business, devolved and local government, and communities to bring about change. We will take initial steps to confront poverty by introducing free breakfast clubs in every primary school, protecting renters from arbitrary eviction, slashing fuel poverty, banning exploitative zero hours contracts, and improving support to help people get into good work. Our system of state, private, and workplace pensions provide the basis for security in retirement. Labour is committed to reviewing Universal Credit so that it makes work pay and tackles poverty. We want to end mass dependence on emergency food parcels, which is a moral scar on our society.

bearing_set.reason: Slashing fuel poverty, ending reliance on emergency food parcels, and Universal Credit reform directly target households' ability to afford energy and food — core cost-of-living essentials.
Protecting renters from arbitrary eviction directly affects housing security and tenure, a core indicator of affordable housing access.
Banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, improving employment support, and reforming Universal Credit to 'make work pay' directly affect job security, quality, and in-work income.
Free breakfast clubs in every primary school directly affect educational attainment and opportunity, particularly for disadvantaged pupils who are most affected by food insecurity.

Multiple new spending commitments (universal breakfast clubs, fuel poverty reduction, employment support) carry significant fiscal costs; no funding mechanism is stated, making the 'funded vs borrowed' indicator materially affected.

The entire policy is explicitly targeted at the lowest-income households and children; measures (UC reform, zero-hours ban, fuel poverty reduction) mechanistically compress the income gap between poorest and rest.

membership_note: This is a broad multi-measure policy cluster spanning housing, energy, work, education and welfare, each with a distinct concrete mechanism on a different fundamental; the six bearings each have a named indicator and non-negligible effect.
